title: Hvar with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Ferries, Rules & Costs
metaDescription: Hvar with a dog in 2027: dog beaches, ferry and catamaran rules, hotel pet fees, summer heat, best months, vet basics and EU pet passport rules.
content:
## Is Hvar dog-friendly?

Hvar is workable with a dog, but it is not a destination built around dogs. The island has no fenced dog parks, no beach showers for dogs and few large-dog hotel rooms. Dogs are tolerated almost everywhere outdoors, and the island's pebble beaches, pine-shaded coves and coast paths suit them. The main limits are heat, hot stone surfaces and hotel pet policies.

## Dog beaches on Hvar (plaža za pse)

Croatian signs for dog beaches read *plaža za pse* or *pasja plaža*. Hvar has two commonly named ones.

- **Majerovica** lies west of Hvar Town harbour. It is a pebble beach reached on foot along the promenade, past hotels and small bathing coves. It is the most convenient option for anyone staying in town.
- **Zarače** is a pebble bay on the south coast, 6 km from Hvar Town. It has a designated dog section and a nearby restaurant. It has no showers or fresh water, so bring water and shade for the dog. You need your own car or a water taxi.

Only one of these is likely to be signed as a dog area in any given season. Check the signage on arrival, since listings differ on the exact setup of both beaches.

### Are dogs allowed on other beaches?

In general, yes. Most Croatian beaches allow dogs unless a sign prohibits them. Hotel beaches, beach clubs and the central Vela plaža in Hvar Town often restrict dogs, and municipal rules can change by season. Remote coves such as Mekićevica, Dubovica and Pokonji Dol suit dogs better. Some are reachable only by boat or on foot, so carry water.

Dogs must be kept under control and owners must clean up after them. Lunchtime visits on pebble beaches are not advisable in July and August, as the stones become very hot.

## Hvar Town old town, restaurants and shops

Dogs on a lead can walk the old town, the riva and the main square. The polished stone paving gets very hot in summer and is slippery, so walk dogs before 9:00 or after 19:30. Many konobas let dogs lie by the table on outdoor terraces. Indoor dining is left to the owner of each venue, and dogs are barred from hotel restaurants and spas at several properties. Ask before sitting down. Dogs are generally refused in food shops and bakeries. Buses on the island carry dogs at the driver's discretion.

## National parks and nature areas

Hvar has no national park. Hiking is on marked paths in the interior, the Stari Grad Plain (UNESCO-listed) and the coast near Zarače. The nearest national parks on the mainland, such as Krka and Paklenica, have their own leash rules and swimming restrictions. Check each park's current rules before a day trip with a dog.

## Ferries and catamarans to Hvar with a dog

Car ferries are the easiest way to travel with a dog. On Jadrolinija, dogs over 8 kg travel free on the open deck, muzzled and on a lead. Small pets under 8 kg in a waterproof carrier up to 45 x 35 x 25 cm can go in the salon.

Catamarans are stricter. Jadrolinija catamarans carry dogs only in designated boxes on the open deck, with a fee and a mandatory reservation. Krilo and TP Line require a muzzle and lead, with kennels at roughly €12 or a carrier. Guide dogs are exempt from the muzzle rule. Large dogs on catamarans need a deck box, and Krilo only takes them if the technical conditions are met.

Drivers should take the Jadrolinija car ferry from Split to Stari Grad, a 20 km drive from Hvar Town, or the Drvenik–Sućuraj line, where dogs are also free on the open deck. For a large dog, the car ferry beats any catamaran. Book the dog's place on a catamaran at the same time as your ticket.

## What accommodation charges for a dog

Private apartments and villas typically charge €10–€20 per night, or nothing, and they are the most flexible option for medium and large dogs. Hotels charge more and set tight limits:

- Riva Marina Hvar Hotel: €40 per night, 10 kg limit, one pet per room, not allowed in dining areas or the spa.
- Amfora Hvar Grand Beach Resort: about €40 per day plus a one-off €100 cleaning fee, dogs under 8 kg.

Several other hotels, including Adriana Hvar Spa Hotel and PLACES Hvar by Valamar in Stari Grad, list pets as welcome. Policies vary by room type, so confirm weight limits in writing. Campsites such as the one at Vira usually take dogs for a small daily fee.

## Where to stay with a dog

Stari Grad, Jelsa and Vrboska are calmer and easier day to day, with more shade and fewer crowds. Hvar Town has the best choice of places to eat and stay but is noisy and hot in peak season. A ground-floor apartment near a coast path is the best base for a dog. Skip the central Hvar Town hotels if the dog is over 10 kg, because most refuse large dogs.

## Summer heat and the best months to visit

July and August regularly reach 30–35°C, and pavement and stone temperatures are far higher. Never leave a dog in a parked car. Walk early and late, rest in the shade at midday, and carry water.

The best months are May, June, September and October. Sea temperatures reach swimmable levels from June, and October is calm and less crowded. April is cool and quiet, and many seasonal places are closed.

## Vet basics

Hvar has limited vet capacity, especially outside the main season. Larger clinics with full diagnostics are in Split on the mainland. Save the number of a Split emergency clinic before travelling.

Common health risks in coastal Croatia are ticks, sandflies (leishmaniasis) and heartworm. Ask your home vet about tick prevention and a sandfly collar before you leave. Pack the vaccination record, any regular medication, a dog first-aid kit and a collapsible water bowl. Do not let dogs drink seawater or swim in very hot conditions.

## EU pet passport rules for driving to Croatia

The requirements for dogs entering Croatia are:

1. A microchip (ISO 11784/11785).
2. A valid rabies vaccination, given at least 21 days before travel.
3. An EU pet passport, or an animal health certificate if the dog comes from outside the EU.

Tapeworm treatment is not required for Croatia. It is only needed when re-entering Finland, Ireland, Malta, Northern Ireland or Norway. The limit is five pets per traveller. Dogs from non-EU countries must enter via a designated point with the correct documents. Check current rules with the national authority before departure.

## Verdict: how dog-friendly is Hvar?

**Hvar is 3.5 out of 5 for dogs.** The island is good for small and medium dogs and for owners who rent apartments in Stari Grad or Jelsa. The scenery, coves and walking are excellent. Large dogs are harder on catamarans and in hotels, and the summer heat is the biggest risk. Plan a trip in May–June or September–October, take the car ferry to Stari Grad, and use Majerovica or Zarače as the dog beaches.

faq.question: Is there a dog beach in Hvar?
faq.answer: Yes. Majerovica, west of Hvar Town harbour, and Zarače, 6 km from town on the south coast, are the commonly named dog beaches. Both are pebble beaches with minimal facilities. Check the signs on arrival.

faq.question: Can dogs travel on the ferry to Hvar?
faq.answer: Yes. On Jadrolinija car ferries, dogs travel free on the open deck with a muzzle and lead. Catamarans are stricter: Jadrolinija uses reserved deck boxes for a fee, and Krilo and TP Line allow small dogs in carriers up to 8 kg or kennels.

faq.question: How much do hotels in Hvar charge for a dog?
faq.answer: Hotels typically charge about €40 per night, sometimes with a one-off cleaning fee of around €100. Many cap dogs at 8–10 kg. Private apartments are cheaper, usually €10–€20 per night, and often take larger dogs.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Hvar with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June, September and October are the best months, with milder weather and fewer people. July and August often reach 30–35°C, and the stone surfaces are too hot for paws at midday.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia?
faq.answer: A dog needs a microchip, a valid rabies vaccination given at least 21 days before travel, and an EU pet passport or health certificate. Tapeworm treatment is not required for Croatia.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed in restaurants in Hvar?
faq.answer: Dogs are usually welcome on outdoor terraces and at konobas where the owner allows it. Indoor access depends on the venue, and hotel restaurants and spas often refuse dogs. Ask before you sit down.

quickAnswer: Hvar is moderately dog-friendly. Dogs are welcome on most beaches without a no-dogs sign, with Majerovica and Zarače as the named dog spots. Car ferries take dogs free on the open deck, hotels charge about €40 per night, and May–June and September–October are the best months. Hvar Town is hot and busy in summer.
